title: Letters and Promise
premise: For ten years, Yara Nystrom has received unsigned letters at her grandfather's decommissioned lighthouse on the Norwegian coast—letters that became the spine of her novels and the quiet love story she never admitted to living. When Elias Vinter, the terminally ill man who wrote them, moves into the neighboring cottage under a false name to finally see the life he shaped from a distance, Yara begins to suspect her reclusive new neighbor is more than he claims. As winter closes in and Elias's health fails, both must decide whether truth is worth destroying the delicate fiction that kept them safe. In the end, Yara learns his identity just as the last train of the season departs—and instead of letting him slip away to die alone as he planned, she asks him to stay, choosing a short, honest love over a long, protected silence.
about_author: Ulyana Zhou is a former maritime archivist who spent three winters cataloguing correspondence in coastal lighthouse stations before turning to fiction full-time. She writes from a converted signal house in northern Norway, where the trains still run only twice a day.

chapters.title: The Tenth Winter
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. On the anniversary of the first letter's arrival, Yara rereads a decade of correspondence while struggling with her publisher's demand for a 'real' ending to her next novel. The beat: longing disguised as routine.

chapters.title: Smoke Next Door
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A moving van arrives at the long-empty cottage beside the lighthouse; its occupant, 'Mr. Vinter,' is polite, pale, and strangely familiar with her habits. The beat: unease threaded with curiosity.

chapters.title: A Man Made of Margins
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias unpacks ten years of unsent drafts, rationing his remaining months into small observations of Yara through frosted windows. The beat: tenderness poisoned by secrecy.

chapters.title: Borrowed Weather
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A storm strands them together in the lighthouse when Elias offers to help secure the lamp room; he knows the staircase by heart. The beat: intimacy that feels like déjà vu.

chapters.title: What the Letters Never Said
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Flashback to the accident a decade ago that bound him to silent penance—the reason he began writing and why he believes he forfeited the right to be known. The beat: guilt as origin story.

chapters.title: Tea at Odd Hours
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Neighboring rituals form: shared tea, arguments about her manuscript's cowardly heroine, and Yara noticing Elias quotes phrases only her letters contain. The beat: suspicion blooming into hope.

chapters.title: The Doctor's Envelope
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Hospital results arrive; Elias burns them unread, then retrieves them from the stove, keeping time now measured in appointments he refuses. The beat: denial hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Manuscript for One Reader
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. She gives Elias her unfinished novel; his marginal notes are so precisely her that she tests him with a fabricated detail from a letter—and he corrects it. The beat: the trap closing gently.

chapters.title: Confrontation in the Lamp Room
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara accuses Elias of being the letter writer; he denies it too smoothly, and she retreats, ashamed of wanting it to be true. The beat: hope wounded by self-doubt.

chapters.title: The Train Timetable
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias books a one-way ticket south for the season's final departure, planning to disappear before Yara can confirm what she already knows. The beat: escape rehearsed as mercy.

chapters.title: Snowbound
chapters.summary: Dual POV alternating scenes. A blizzard knocks out power; they share candles, stories, and one almost-confession each, interrupted by the storm itself. The beat: closeness without permission.

chapters.title: Grandfather's Ledger
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Sorting her late grandfather's papers, Yara finds a receipt linking Elias Vinter to the lighthouse's past—and to the night her parents' boat was lost. The beat: love and grief colliding.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Full revelation of the wreck: Elias survived it; Yara's father did not, and the letters were penance addressed to the granddaughter left behind. The beat: shame laid completely bare.

chapters.title: Return Address
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Armed with the ledger, Yara confronts Elias with every letter's postmark mapped against his old addresses; he cannot lie anymore. The beat: the fiction shattering.

chapters.title: Anger, Properly Kept
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara banishes him, grieving twice over—a father and a decade of imagined love, both built on omission. The beat: rage as fidelity to the dead.

chapters.title: Last Letter, Unsent
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias writes the confession he should have delivered years ago, seals it, and slides it under her door before packing for the final train. The beat: honesty arriving too late, or exactly on time.

chapters.title: What Survives a Wreck
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Reading his confession, Yara understands the letters were never evasion but survival—his and hers both—and races the clock as the station bell rings. The beat: forgiveness chosen under pressure.

chapters.title: The Last Train Leaves
chapters.summary: Dual POV. At the platform, Elias boards; Yara arrives as it pulls away—and finds him still standing on the platform beside his abandoned suitcase. The beat: the choice made visible.

chapters.title: Stay After the Light
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara asks him plainly to stay—not to be forgiven, but to be known; Elias, terrified of being witnessed dying, says yes anyway. The beat: courage over protection.

chapters.title: Days Measured in Small Hours
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They live openly at last: writing together, lighting the lamp for passing boats, loving without the alibi of anonymity. The beat: joy that does not deny sorrow.

chapters.title: Spring Tide
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Elias dies at dawn with the lamp lit and Yara's hand in his, leaving instructions that his letters be published alongside her finished novel. The beat: grief transmuted into legacy.

chapters.title: Letters and Promise
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, epilogue. A year later, the co-published book sits in the lighthouse window; a new letter arrives—from a young reader who found it—and Yara answers. The beat: the cycle renewed, love outlasting its keeper.
